justifications.functional_suitability: Customer/Broker Portal satisfies R-01 for online submissions. Adjuster Workstation and Adjuster BFF fulfill R-02 for adjuster workflows. Incremental migration (R-03) is handled via the Claim Migration Manager and Claim Routing & Feature Flag Component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-2s response times (R-05) against 5s mainframe latency are achieved using the Adjuster BFF Read-Model Cache Manager and PostgreSQL Read Replica. Asynchronous decoupling via Integration Worker and Azure Service Bus avoids blocking adjuster screens and protects batch windows.
justifications.compatibility: Coexistence with the legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe is explicitly managed via the Anti-Corruption Layer Gateway, Integration Worker Transformation Engine, and MFT/asynchronous messaging. Microsoft Entra ID seamlessly integrates for enterprise SSO via OIDC/OAuth2.
justifications.usability: Distinct, purpose-built interfaces serve each user group: Customer/Broker Portal (Next.js UI) serves policyholders and brokers, while Adjuster Workstation (React SPA with real-time SSE updates) provides an optimized workspace for claims adjusters.
justifications.reliability: R-04 consistency is ensured via Idempotency & Audit Manager, Outbox/Retry Dispatcher Component, and Azure Service Bus. Mainframe fault isolation is maintained using Polly circuit breakers in Integration Worker and APIM Backend Circuit Breaker.
justifications.security: Single Sign-On (R-07) is implemented using Microsoft Entra ID, Token Validator Component, and Authentication Handler. Audit compliance is enforced through Idempotency & Audit Manager and PostgreSQL's Audit & Compliance Log Store with pgaudit.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 one-day rollback is enabled by the Claim Routing & Feature Flag Component and Feature/Kill-Switch Component. Clear bounded contexts, separation of Adjuster BFF from Core Claims Domain, and an Anti-Corruption Layer isolate legacy changes.
justifications.portability: Hybrid connectivity between azure-westeurope and on-premises is addressed with Secure Hybrid Ingress and ExpressRoute/VPN. However, heavy reliance on proprietary Azure APIM XML policies and Azure-specific PaaS services slightly impairs cross-cloud replaceability.

PERF-01.justification: The Adjuster BFF queries a dedicated PostgreSQL Read Model and Cache Store rather than synchronously querying the mainframe, shielding adjuster workstation screens from legacy 5-second response times.
sensitivity_points: Read cache invalidation and synchronization lag from mainframe updates
tradeoffs: Increased eventual consistency window in exchange for sub-2s adjuster screen loads

PERF-02.justification: Customer submissions are buffered via Azure Service Bus and processed asynchronously through the Integration Worker, preventing submission spikes from spilling over into the mainframe's nightly batch window.
sensitivity_points: Queue capacity and message consumption throttling rates during peak end-of-month volume
tradeoffs: Immediate submission acknowledgment versus deferred legacy mainframe ingestion

AVAIL-01.justification: Service Bus queues decouple online claims ingress from legacy availability, while the Integration Worker Outbox/Retry Dispatcher and Polly Circuit Breaker hold and forward submissions once batch processing completes.
sensitivity_points: Retention limits and dead-letter handling in Azure Service Bus during maintenance
tradeoffs: Queue storage cost and retry overhead versus high continuous platform availability

AVAIL-02.justification: The Outbox/Retry Dispatcher and Idempotency & Audit Manager prevent duplicates and message loss. However, bidirectional reconciliation logic and conflict resolution between DB2 and PostgreSQL are not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: Reliable idempotency key generation and duplicate detection across hybrid boundaries
tradeoffs: Strict deduplication and transactional outbox overhead versus data consistency guarantees

MOD-01.justification: Incremental migrations and rapid rollbacks are directly supported by Claim Routing & Feature Flags, the Claim Migration Manager, and the Integration Worker Feature/Kill-Switch, enabling one-day switch-back.
sensitivity_points: Granularity and synchronization latency of dynamic feature flags and routing rules
tradeoffs: Operational complexity of maintaining dual routing rules versus zero-downtime migration rollback

MOD-02.justification: Mainframe dependencies are completely isolated behind the Anti-Corruption Layer, Integration Worker, and BFF. Decommissioning the mainframe requires retiring integration adapters without touching adjuster or customer user interfaces.
sensitivity_points: Strict preservation of frontend contracts when backend migration dependencies are severed
tradeoffs: Initial abstraction and ACL development effort versus frictionless legacy mainframe retirement

SEC-01.justification: APIM Token Validator and Entra ID enforce identity, while the Audit & Compliance Log Store records actions. However, fine-grained multi-tenant relationship authorization between brokers and policyholders is not explicitly modeled.
sensitivity_points: Policy enforcement point placement for data-level ownership checks across claims
tradeoffs: Fine-grained claim ownership validation latency versus broad tenant isolation

SEC-02.justification: Centralized Microsoft Entra ID handles user offboarding for cloud interfaces. Revoking mainframe-specific access within 15 minutes depends on external AD synchronization with legacy security systems, which is not fully elaborated.
sensitivity_points: Token TTL duration and synchronization frequency between Entra ID and RACF
tradeoffs: Short token lifetimes or token revocation checks versus token validation performance
